title: The grapes
subtitle: Ripe reds and native whites
objectives: Explain the role of Alicante Bouschet

steps.title: Reds
steps.body: Aragonez, Tempranillo, gives red fruit and body. Trincadeira gives spice, herbs and freshness, but is sensitive to rot. Alicante Bouschet, a French red-fleshed grape, called a teinturier, gives deep colour and structure; it found its best home here. Castelão, Syrah and Touriga Nacional are also common. Reds are ripe, round and generous.

steps.title: Whites
steps.body: Antão Vaz, from Vidigueira, is the main white: ripe tropical fruit and body, tolerant of heat. Arinto adds acidity; Roupeiro adds aroma. Blends of the three are common. White wines are a growing share, especially from cooler sites.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.
steps.explanation: Alentejo blends balance ripeness and freshness.

steps.body: Alicante Bouschet is one of the few grapes with red flesh. That's why wines from it are so deeply coloured.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Aragonez, Trincadeira and Alicante Bouschet lead the reds
Antão Vaz leads the whites, with Arinto for acidity
